correctness.rationale: The free Fourier energies are 2J cos((2πl+phi)/N); their monic characteristic polynomial is 2J^N[T_N(z/(2J))-cos(phi)]. Cyclic translation makes all diagonal cofactors equal, so adding the absorbing site adds i gamma/N times the free polynomial derivative, including at poles by polynomial identity. Independently, at the protected flux put E=2J cos(q), and write the free polynomial locally as the product of the two crossing factors and the remaining factor R, with R(E) nonzero. The secular derivative in z there is (2i gamma/N)R(E), proving simplicity. At fixed z=E the two detuned free energies have opposite slopes ±2J sin(q)/N; the free part of the secular polynomial therefore contributes -(2J sin(q)/N)^2 R(E) delta². The cofactor is flux independent (deleting the absorbing site leaves a path with gauge-removable phases). Solving the implicit equation gives -i 2J² sin²(q)/(gamma N) times delta². Flux enters through cos(phi), and uniqueness gives evenness and thus O(delta⁴). The real shift is at most O(delta⁴), not necessarily a nonzero quartic term. A real eigenvalue forces the trap amplitude to vanish by the dissipative identity; off 0 or pi the free spectrum is simple and each Fourier eigenvector has nonzero trap amplitude. Unpaired band-edge modes are likewise not dark. The probability rate is twice the eigenvalue linewidth in this convention. This is fixed-parameter and mode-local; the supplied numerical checks were inspected, not executed.

evidence: The exact site-transfer equation precedes and is independent of Heinrichs's later real random disorder approximation; each transfer matrix has determinant one for complex site potentials as well.
Longhi treats a continuum ring, Gou et al. a lossy triangle coupled to leads, and Burke et al. an open tight-binding chain with an imaginary impurity.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The discrete general-site transfer equation, rather than the continuum, transport or open-chain results, covers the needed secular equation. Its one-defect reduction holds at any nonzero fixed loss, not just perturbatively in the defect.

evidence: The one-site specialization gives T_N(x)-cos(phi)+i gamma U_{N-1}(x)/(2J)=0. At x=cos(q), U_{N-1} vanishes simply with derivative -N cos(Nq)/sin²(q), while T_N'=0. The flux increment is cos(phi_*) delta²/2.
A real root requires U_{N-1}(x)=0, whose roots are cos(jπ/N); then T_N(x)=±1.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Implicit division by the simple imaginary derivative gives exactly the coefficient, with an even branch because the right side depends only on cos(phi). The real-root condition gives the stated dark-flux restriction; dissipativity supplies the sign. These require no additional spectral mechanism beyond the earlier exact equation.

evidence: Heinrichs derives tr(product of site transfer matrices)=2 cos(total dimensionless flux) for the same nearest-neighbor cycle with site potentials. The flux phases inside each transfer matrix can be removed by a common similarity.
Resultary 9c2164f9c4e0 explicitly states both the secular identity and the half-flux quadratic coefficient for an even ring, with absorber -i gamma/2 instead of -i gamma.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: After normalizing hopping and gauging the phases to the boundary, write M=[[2x,-1],[1,0]]. The absorber replaces just one factor by M+(i gamma/J)E11. The trace is 2T_N(x)+(i gamma/J)(M^{N-1})_11=2T_N(x)+(i gamma/J)U_{N-1}(x). Use T_N'=N U_{N-1}. The two Resultary conventions match by doubling the parameter of the -i gamma/2 model.

originality.rationale: The bound coefficient is not stated verbatim in the inspected early literature, but it is a mechanical specialization of an earlier exact transfer-matrix equation. Heinrichs, arXiv:cond-mat/0106437v1, Eqs. (12)–(18), gives the exact trace condition for a tight-binding ring with general diagonal site potentials, before making a weak-disorder expansion. That derivation uses unimodularity and the linear recurrence, not reality of the potentials, and therefore extends algebraically to a single imaginary potential. The single rank-one insertion produces precisely the bound secular polynomial, from which simplicity, evenness, the coefficient and the restriction on real eigenvalues follow directly. This failure is based on an inspected governing result, not on the unavailable 1996 article or on dating a later equivalent catalogue entry.
residual_risks: The exact chronology of related indexed derivations is not established beyond their catalogue dates.

value.rationale: The mode-resolved linewidth is physically useful, and its normalization is worth getting right. As the contribution claimed here, however, it is the direct simple-root expansion of a prior general spectral condition with one rank-one matrix insertion. The symmetry and no-dark conclusion follow from that same specialized equation. No genuinely distinct mathematical remainder (such as a uniform detuning/loss limit or survival theorem) is part of the frozen claim.
